methods.label: Find an equal leg from the perimeter
methods.explanation:
Let each equal leg have length \(a>0\). The Pythagorean theorem gives the hypotenuse as \(a\sqrt2\), so the perimeter condition is
\[
(2+\sqrt2)a=2p.
\]
Here \(p>0\), since the triangle has positive perimeter. Rationalizing the positive denominator gives
\[
a=\frac{2p}{2+\sqrt2}
=\frac{2p(2-\sqrt2)}{4-2}
=(2-\sqrt2)p.
\]
The legs are perpendicular, so one is a base and the other its height. The area is therefore
\[
\frac{a^2}{2}
=\frac{(2-\sqrt2)^2p^2}{2}
=(3-2\sqrt2)p^2.
\]
The answer is choice C.
